jobs.title: Financial Planning Analyst
jobs.description:
Advisors · RIAs · Portfolio Workflows

About the job

PortfolioFuture is an independent fund discovery and intelligence company. We use empirical research to discover, evaluate, and rank ETFs and mutual funds, and identify where they can credibly compete for allocations in portfolios.

Our research connects more than 10,000 funds with institutional investors, 23,000+ advisory firms, and 400,000+ financial advisors, supporting fund discovery, portfolio analytics, and asset-manager distribution intelligence.

As a Financial Planning Analyst, you will study how financial advisors and wealth managers evaluate the funds PortfolioFuture identifies. The role covers advisor research, portfolio workflows, fund consideration, and the development of market intelligence used across PortfolioFuture.

You will speak with advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals to understand what makes a fund worth investigating, what keeps it out of a portfolio, and how those judgments differ across firms and client types.

What you’ll work on

• Speak with financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth-management professionals about funds identified through PortfolioFuture’s research.
• Study how advisors compare competing ETFs and mutual funds and what makes a fund worth further consideration.
• Document the recurring questions, objections, and concerns that come up around specific funds and investment strategies.
• Research how advisors judge a fund’s strategy, positioning, fees, track record, and role in a portfolio.
• Compare how different advisors evaluate the same investment product.
• Turn qualitative conversations into structured market intelligence the rest of PortfolioFuture can act on.
• Identify gaps between how a fund manager describes a strategy and how the wealth-management market understands it.
• Study how a fund enters an advisor’s consideration set and what moves it from awareness to real due diligence.
• Work with PortfolioFuture’s substitution and decomposition research so advisor conversations stay grounded in evidence.
• Use large language models and other tools to organize, summarize, and analyze qualitative research at scale.
• Share what you learn with research, product, and distribution teams so findings reach the people who can use them.
• Test whether the patterns you observe hold across firm size, client type, and market environment.

What we’re looking for

• Background in finance, economics, business, wealth management, communications, or a related field.
• Strong interest in financial advisors, RIAs, wealth management, ETFs, and mutual funds.
• Ability to conduct thoughtful professional conversations and ask useful follow-up questions.
• Ability to understand an investment product well enough to discuss it with experienced advisors.
• Strong listening skills and the ability to identify patterns across many different conversations.
• Ability to turn qualitative feedback into clear, structured written findings.
• Comfort reaching out to and speaking with experienced wealth-management professionals.
• Ability to communicate what you learned clearly, including what you are not yet sure about.
• Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, investment product distribution, or practice management is useful but not required.
• Experience with research interviews, qualitative analysis, CRM data, or survey design is a plus.

PortfolioFuture research

Fund Substitution identifies ETFs and mutual funds that can serve similar portfolio roles, using return similarity, relative performance, tracking error, and fees.

Fund Decomposition separates returns explained by investable market exposures from residual performance, evaluating replication quality, residual alpha, and risk.

Fund Opportunity ranks ETFs and mutual funds across four dimensions: Similar Fund Ranking, Addressable Market, Pure Alpha, and Diversification Benefits.

PortfolioFuture’s research is independent. Commercial relationships do not affect which funds are surfaced, how they rank, or the conclusions reached.

jobs.description:
Role:
The Director of Real-World Data & Epidemiology (RWD & Epi) Analytics leads the design, execution, and communication of observational studies using diverse RWD sources.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with asset leaders to plan and report epidemiologic studies, including feasibility assessments, study design, data analysis, and reporting.
Conduct survival and economic modeling to support health technology assessments (HTA).
Manage study execution, including data management, analysis programming, and quality assurance, ensuring regulatory compliance.
Present findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, translating complex data into actionable insights.
Evaluate emerging data modalities and integrate AI-driven analytics into evidence-generation processes.
Mentor scientists and programmers, fostering technical growth and best practices.
Develop standardized processes for study execution, data management, and infrastructure evolution in collaboration with data and AI teams.
Contribute to strategic departmental initiatives and represent the team on key projects.

Qualifications & Skills

Graduate degree (PhD or Master’s) in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Public Health, or related field.
Over 10 years of experience in real-world evidence generation and epidemiology analytics.
Expertise in observational study design, statistical methods (e.g., survival analysis, causal inference), and RWD evaluation.
Proficiency in statistical programming (SAS, R, Python) and AI/ML frameworks.
Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
Preferred experience in oncology and a strategic mindset for commercial and clinical contexts.
Proven research accomplishments with peer-reviewed publications.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in fast-paced environments, demonstrating proactivity and enthusiasm.

Additional Details:
The role offers flexible work arrangements away from the office, with a competitive salary range. Benefits include health plans, retirement contributions, paid time off, wellness support, and other perks. The position involves leadership in analytics, study design, and infrastructure development within a collaborative, innovative environment dedicated to advancing cancer and serious disease treatments.

jobs.title: Analyst, Executive Operations & AI Enablement - Commercial & CFS Procurement
jobs.description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.

Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is seeking a high-caliber, early-career professional for the position of Executive Operations & AI Enablement Analyst, within Commercial & Corporate Functions & Services (CFS) Procurement. The role serves as a strategic enabler and force multiplier to the Vice President of Commercial & CFS Procurement, blending executive support, project coordination, leadership-team enablement, and hands-on digital and AI tooling into a single, integrated position. As the Executive Operations Analyst, you will operate with a high degree of autonomy and direct exposure to executive decision-making. This is a talent-accelerator role offering direct exposure to executive leadership, enterprise-level strategy, supplier negotiations, and cross-functional execution, combined with a mandate to build with AI at the leading edge of how work gets done.

You will own the VP’s calendar end-to-end — issuing meeting invitations on the VP’s behalf, negotiating scheduling directly with internal senior leaders and external supplier executives, and orchestrating scheduling campaigns spanning the US, Europe, and Asia. You will produce daily and weekly executive intelligence products (day summaries and an interactive leadership dashboard) that keep the VP and Leadership Team focused on the highest-value priorities, and you will actively build and deploy AI and digital solutions — from automated reporting to working prototypes of business tools — that raise the productivity of the entire organization.

Major Responsibilities And Accountabilities

Executive Time & Operating Rhythm

Own and autonomously orchestrate the VP’s calendar end-to-end scheduling, sequencing, and prioritization of meetings, including sending invitations directly from the VP’s calendar.
Anticipate conflicts, proactively flag trade-offs with options and a recommendation, and resolve scheduling constraints across global time zones.
Coordinate scheduling directly with external counterparties — strategic suppliers, banking and supply-chain-finance partners, and consulting firms — with professionalism and discretion.
Execute large-scale scheduling campaigns (e.g., organizing 75+ one-off 1 1s across an extended global team; standing 1 1 cadences with direct reports), tracking completion and escalating only genuine decision points.
Produce a daily executive day summary for the VP a synthesis of the day’s meetings, preparation needs, pinch points, and priorities.

Meeting Effectiveness & Follow-Through

Prepare agendas, pre-reads, executive briefs, and synthesis materials for leadership meetings and key forums.
Capture meeting minutes, decisions, action items, and owners; drive closed-loop follow-up so commitments are executed.
Proactively chase inputs, send reminders (e.g., logistics, registrations, travel bookings), unblock progress, and maintain execution momentum.
Draft professional communications on behalf of the VP with sound judgment and discretion.

Executive Reporting & Leadership Dashboards

Build, maintain, and publish a weekly interactive executive dashboard consolidating leadership updates, initiative status, and key metrics for the VP and Leadership Team.
Consolidate inputs from across Commercial & CFS Procurement into clear, executive-level status reporting.
Continuously improve reporting products based on leadership feedback, iterating week over week.

Project & Leadership Team Coordination

Coordinate and track strategic and operational initiatives across Commercial & CFS Procurement, maintaining action plans, milestones, and dependencies across the VP’s Leadership Team.
Support planning and orchestration of leadership meetings, working sessions (e.g., procurement/budget process-improvement sessions), category strategy reviews, and executive development programs.
Support leadership transitions and onboarding (e.g., establishing meeting cadences and introductions for incoming senior leaders).
Coordinate follow-ups with suppliers and internal teams on behalf of the VP (e.g., payment-terms status requests, negotiation working-session logistics).

Technology, Data & AI Enablement

Actively build with AI configure and operate agentic AI tools (AI coding assistants, agent skills, browser automation) to automate recurring executive workflows such as day summaries, dashboard generation, and scheduling support.
Rapidly prototype lightweight digital tools for business problems (e.g., a guided data-intake console built on real procurement PO-level data to reduce reporting errors), and pressure-test concepts with business owners before wider build-out.
Share AI configurations, skills, and best practices with the VP and the wider team to accelerate organizational AI adoption and productivity.
Build and maintain trackers, templates, and dashboards (Excel, PowerPoint, HTML/low-code tools); continuously identify opportunities to simplify and optimize workflows.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Minimum education of a bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, analytics, economics, supply chain, or a related field is required.
Minimum of two (2) years of professional experience; strong maturity, curiosity, and learning agility is required.
Demonstrated analytical ability and problem-solving skills through academic, professional, or experiential achievement.
Demonstrated AI and digital fluency, with evidence of having built or automated something real (e.g., automation, scripting, low-code or web prototyping).
Ability to synthesize complex information into executive-ready insights.
Experience supporting executives, coordinating projects, or working in procurement, supply chain, finance, or strategy/operations environments preferred.

We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Compensation Overview

Princeton - NJ - US $74,630 - $90,434

The starting pay range(s) listed above is for full-time employees (FTE). You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Final compensation is guided by pay equity principles and applicable employment laws. Compensation programs are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be adjusted over time to reflect evolving market factors, and individual, team or Company performance.

Benefits

Subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans then in effect, you may be eligible to participate in our comprehensive benefit plans – including wellbeing support, retirement and financial protection benefits, and insurance offerings (medical, dental, vision, life and disability).

U.S.-based exempt employees are eligible for Flexible Time Off (FTO), which provides paid time off without a set accrual limit, subject to manager approval, along with 11 paid company holidays each year.

Non-exempt employees, RayzeBio employees, and employees located in Puerto Rico receive 160 hours of paid vacation annually for new hires (subject to manager approval), 11 paid company holidays, and 3 optional holidays.

Depending on eligibility, employees may also have access to additional time-off benefits, including paid sick leave, up to two paid volunteer days per year, summer hours flexibility, and leaves of absence for medical, personal, parental, caregiver, bereavement, or military needs. Eligible employees also enjoy an annual Global Shutdown between Christmas Day and New Year's Day.

U.S.-based job seekers can explore full benefit offerings at https //careers.bms.com/benefits

How We Work

Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at https //careers.bms.com/ways-of-working.

Supporting People With Disabilities

BMS is dedicated to ensuring that people with disabilities can excel through a transparent recruitment process, reasonable workplace accommodations/adjustments and ongoing support in their roles. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. If you require reasonable accommodations/adjustments in completing this application, or in any part of the recruitment process, direct your inquiries to adastaffingsupport@bms.com. Visit careers.bms.com/eeo-accessibility to access our complete Equal Employment Opportunity statement.

Candidate Rights

BMS will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, pursuant to applicable laws in your area.

For roles based in Los Angeles County only If you live in or expect to work from Los Angeles County if hired for this position, please visit this page for important additional information https //careers.bms.com/california-residents/

Data Protection

We will never request payments, financial information, or social security numbers during our application or recruitment process. Learn more about protecting yourself at https //careers.bms.com/fraud-protection.

Any data processed in connection with role applications will be treated in accordance with applicable data privacy policies and regulations.

If this posting is missing required information required by local law or incorrect, contact BMS at TAEnablement@bms.comwith the Job Title and Requisition number. Do not send application-related inquiries to this email. To check your application status, please login to your Candidate Home Account.

You will produce daily and weekly executive intelligence products (day summaries and an interactive leadership dashboard) that keep the VP and Leadership Team focused on the highest-value priorities, and you will actively build and deploy AI and digital solutions — from automated reporting to working prototypes of business tools — that raise the productivity of the entire organization.

Major Responsibilities And Accountabilities

Executive Time & Operating Rhythm

Own and autonomously orchestrate the VP’s calendar end-to-end scheduling, sequencing, and prioritization of meetings, including sending invitations directly from the VP’s calendar.
Anticipate conflicts, proactively flag trade-offs with options and a recommendation, and resolve scheduling constraints across global time zones.
Coordinate scheduling directly with external counterparties — strategic suppliers, banking and supply-chain-finance partners, and consulting firms — with professionalism and discretion.
Execute large-scale scheduling campaigns (e.g., organizing 75+ one-off 1 1s across an extended global team; standing 1 1 cadences with direct reports), tracking completion and escalating only genuine decision points.
Produce a daily executive day summary for the VP a synthesis of the day’s meetings, preparation needs, pinch points, and priorities.

Meeting Effectiveness & Follow-Through

Prepare agendas, pre-reads, executive briefs, and synthesis materials for leadership meetings and key forums.
Capture meeting minutes, decisions, action items, and owners; drive closed-loop follow-up so commitments are executed.
Proactively chase inputs, send reminders (e.g., logistics, registrations, travel bookings), unblock progress, and maintain execution momentum.
Draft professional communications on behalf of the VP with sound judgment and discretion.

Executive Reporting & Leadership Dashboards

Build, maintain, and publish a weekly interactive executive dashboard consolidating leadership updates, initiative status, and key metrics for the VP and Leadership Team.
Consolidate inputs from across Commercial & CFS Procurement into clear, executive-level status reporting.
Continuously improve reporting products based on leadership feedback, iterating week over week.

Project & Leadership Team Coordination

Coordinate and track strategic and operational initiatives across Commercial & CFS Procurement, maintaining action plans, milestones, and dependencies across the VP’s Leadership Team.
Support planning and orchestration of leadership meetings, working sessions (e.g., procurement/budget process-improvement sessions), category strategy reviews, and executive development programs.
Support leadership transitions and onboarding (e.g., establishing meeting cadences and introductions for incoming senior leaders).
Coordinate follow-ups with suppliers and internal teams on behalf of the VP (e.g., payment-terms status requests, negotiation working-session logistics).

Technology, Data & AI Enablement

Actively build with AI configure and operate agentic AI tools (AI coding assistants, agent skills, browser automation) to automate recurring executive workflows such as day summaries, dashboard generation, and scheduling support.
Rapidly prototype lightweight digital tools for business problems (e.g., a guided data-intake console built on real procurement PO-level data to reduce reporting errors), and pressure-test concepts with business owners before wider build-out.
Share AI configurations, skills, and best practices with the VP and the wider team to accelerate organizational AI adoption and productivity.
Build and maintain trackers, templates, and dashboards (Excel, PowerPoint, HTML/low-code tools); continuously identify opportunities to simplify and optimize workflows.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Minimum education of a bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, analytics, economics, supply chain, or a related field is required.
Minimum of two (2) years of professional experience; strong maturity, curiosity, and learning agility is required.
Demonstrated analytical ability and problem-solving skills through academic, professional, or experiential achievement.
Demonstrated AI and digital fluency, with evidence of having built or automated something real (e.g., automation, scripting, low-code or web prototyping).
Ability to synthesize complex information into executive-ready insights.
Experience supporting executives, coordinating projects, or working in procurement, supply chain, finance, or strategy/operations environments preferred.
